title: Citizens march in Kolkata against attacks on bookstalls

tea.why: Protesters marched to condemn recent attacks, vandalism, and arson targeting bookstalls during the Durga Puja festival.
tea.want: Protesters demanded an end to attacks on books, free thinking, and cultural expression.
tea.changed: Oct 31: Hundreds of citizens, writers, activists, and students marched on College Street in Kolkata carrying books in a rally titled 'Walk for Books'.

summary: On October 31, 2026, hundreds of citizens, activists, writers, academics, students, and politicians participated in a march titled 'Walk for Books' at College Street, also known as Boipara, in Kolkata. According to the sources, the participants walked holding books, banners, and posters to protest against recent attacks, vandalism, and arson targeting bookstalls displaying Marxist and progressive literature during the Durga Puja festival. Organisers and participants blamed right-wing groups and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for the incidents. The march took place without political flags or banners, featuring prominent figures from civil society as well as Left party leaders such as Mohammad Salim, Sujan Chakraborty, Biman Bose, and Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) alleged that nearly 300 stalls had been targeted across the state.
demands: Stop attacks on bookstalls and free thinking
Protect the freedom to read, publish, and sell books
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Hundreds of participants joined the 'Walk for Books' march at College Square in Kolkata to protest against bookstall vandalism.
